content_html_sanitized:
Well, unfortunately the public discourse in the UK on cannabis policies is as wretched as I thought last week.

Amsterdam and London: A Tale of Two Cities

 

My headline last week was about Amsterdam and London, because the Mayor’s report did have an accurate description of Dutch cannabis policy, but then stopped without describing the actual results, that de facto legalization of retail sales of cannabis actually works and did not destroy the country.

 

As I said, “Of course, this omission is hardly unique, and of all the absurdities of cannabis prohibition, nothing puzzles me more than the invisibility of The Netherlands. It is not some exotic land, far, far away.”

 

Weirdly, The Guardian, the excellent center left broadsheet carried a well written history of the cannabis debate in the UK with the title “Worried about weed: should London follow New York and decriminalise cannabis?”

 

I said “weirdly” because New York didn’t “decriminalize” cannabis, it legalized it, but made a mess of it, their article did not mention anything about the Dutch experience.

 

However, the Guardian did publish an excellent piece by their columnist Simon Jenkins, saying, Sadiq Khan is right: Britain must decriminalise cannabis – or remain in the dark ages.

 

Marijuananews note: Comparison of safety of London and Amsterdam

 

On the other hand, The London Times speculated, “Have the police effectively decriminalised cannabis already?” Well, in the posher areas, perhaps, because no one who reads The Times ever gets arrested for anything. Simply unthinkable!

 

Meanwhile, the sensationalist Daily Mail’s response was from a Dr. Max Pemberton, with the headline, “Every day, I see the dreadful impact of cannabis - and it's far worse than anyone can possibly imagine. Let me tell you what will REALLY happen if it's decriminalised.”

 

But it is behind a paywall, as well it should be. If they want to pay me, I’ll read it. But will his patients really be worse off if they aren’t threatened with arrest? Dr Max Pemberton

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Pemberton_(doctor)

 

Marijuananews note see: Politicized Psychiatry and the Rehab Rackets

And They Say The Brain Doesn’t Mature Until We Are 25 But That Doesn’t Stop The “Medical Profession” From Giving Children In Foster Care Powerful Psychiatric Drugs

 

Sadly, the coverage of this issue demonstrates the wretched state of the public discourse in the UK, and the “drug” situation there is tragic, especially in Scotland.

 

Scotland’s drug and alcohol deaths remain among the worst in Europe despite increased spending to tackle the problems, a significant report by auditors has found.

 

Scottish drug laws are still controlled by the Parliament in London, so maybe the Scots will be spurred to free themselves from the UK disaster.

 

And how is the Drug War working in Europe?

Very Prohibitionist, reefer madness obsessed, “Sweden is the country with the most drug-induced deaths per million of the population in Europe. In 2018, 81 people died per million inhabitants, ahead of the United Kingdom's 76 drug-induced deaths per million.”

 

To understand the difficulty of the political problem, it is important to note that some of the UK police actually want to go in the opposite direction and reclassify cannabis with heroin, etc.

 

They justify this by confusing the consequences of cannabis use with the consequences of cannabis prohibition. Obviously, the UK government has to address this problem in the politicized police if they are going to have an honest debate on drugs policy.

 

The BBC reports that A Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) says he "fully supports" calls to reclassify cannabis as a Class A drug.

Marijuananews note: with heroin and cocaine, crack cocaine, methamphetamine (crystal meth), Ketamine, etc.

 

Police forces in the west and south west of England have been cracking down on people using recreational drugs, with Dorset PCC David Sidwick this week reiterating calls for cannabis to be upgraded.

 

Wiltshire PCC Philip Wilkinson says he has seen "first-hand" how cannabis cultivation and use are "deeply intertwined with a spectrum of criminal activities" in his county.

 

The Home Office, the UK’s interior ministry, said it has "no intention of reclassifying cannabis from a Class B substance under the Misuse of Drugs Act". (In either direction, apparently.)

 

"From anti-social behaviour and retail theft to more serious offences like modern slavery and human trafficking, cannabis often serves as a gateway drug and funding source for organised crime groups," said Mr Wilkinson.

 

Mr Wilkinson added: "The idea that cannabis is a harmless drug is a misconception. Its cultivation and distribution are often controlled by organised crime networks that exploit vulnerable individuals and perpetuate violence.

 

"County lines operations are the clearest example of how drug-related crime has extended its tentacles into our rural towns and villages. The notion that drug-related crime is only an urban issue is outdated and dangerously naïve."

 

Of course, everything he describes is a result of cannabis prohibition, which is why I keep saying that cannabis prohibition is actually a counterproductive fraud.

 

And apparently I will have to keep saying it. So, I will.
